summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Research design and 24 source leads for Nepal's AI and software export question. Q1: BoP-recorded ICT services exports (NRB BPM6, Nepal FY) and industry-estimated IT exports (survey-based) are defined as separate series and never merged; UNCTADstat (calendar year, derived from NRB) and WTO digitally delivered (modelled) are comparators. The 'unrecorded' share is defined only as a residual after period, coverage (SI vs SJ/SK), channel (freelancer receipts, earnings kept abroad, informal) and gross/net alignment. Q2: segment taxonomy set out; displacement vs growth pending 24A/24C evidence. Q3: workforce design answering 24A's request (NSO NLFS microdata at ISCO-08 4-digit x ISIC, Census 2021 fallback, Online Labour Index and industry freelancer counts kept separate). One WebSearch found only secondary news on industry-estimated IT exports; used as locators only. No values retrieved; all empirical items pending.

findings.claim: Research design Q1: two ICT-export series are kept strictly separate and never merged. Series S1 'BoP-recorded' = NRB BPM6 services credits, telecommunications/computer/information services (EBOPS SI), Nepal fiscal year, NPR current (USD converted at the NRB period-average rate as a separately documented input). Series S2 'industry-estimated' = survey-based IT-export estimates from industry bodies/independent studies (e.g. IIDS-type study), whatever reference period they state. International series S3 (UNCTADstat ICT / digitally deliverable, calendar year) and S4 (WTO digitally delivered, modelled, calendar year) are comparators only.

Recording-gap method: gap = S2 - S1 only after aligning (a) period (FY vs calendar vs survey reference year), (b) coverage (S2 may include ITES/BPO and design/marketing that BPM6 classes as other business services SJ or personal/cultural services SK, not SI), (c) channel (freelancer receipts arriving as personal transfers, via foreign wallets/platform balances kept abroad, or via informal hundi are not SI credits), and (d) gross vs net (platform fees, foreign-kept earnings). Only the residual after (a)-(d) is described as 'unrecorded'; any gap beyond tolerance is escalated to 00B, not adjusted.

Segment taxonomy for Q2 (to be confirmed against S2 composition data): (i) custom software and product engineering; (ii) QA/testing and maintenance; (iii) ITES/BPO: contact centre, data entry/annotation, back-office accounting; (iv) creative: graphic design, video, web design; (v) content/writing/translation; (vi) digital marketing; (vii) data/AI services incl. annotation and model evaluation. Displacement vs growth is assessed per segment from 24A exposure/causal evidence, not asserted in r1.

Workforce definition for Q3: 'qualified IT workforce' = employed persons in ISCO-08 sub-major groups 25 (ICT professionals) and 35 (ICT technicians) plus ITES occupations listed in 24A, split by employer type (IT firm, non-IT employer, self-employed/freelance). Graduate supply (09B) is a flow, employment a stock; the two are not added.

challenges.text: Response to your request: design for IT/BPO employment by ISCO-08 4-digit and IT-export composition is in specific.ict_export_series.workforce_data_design_for_24A. Note: your finding cites 'NLFS 2022/23'; the lead register shows the latest completed NLFS is 2017/18, with NLSS IV 2022/23 (a living-standards survey, different definitions) and NLFS IV fieldwork from FY2024/25. Please re-label the survey you intend to use.

Candidate export segments for Nepal are listed in specific.segment_outlook (nine segments). BPO/freelance segments cannot be sized from BoP because they may fall under SJ/SK or personal transfers; please size global demand at EBOPS SI, SJ and SK separately.
Agree: NRB BPM6 credits are the recorded value. 08A will report the industry-estimated series only as a separate observation and send any gap beyond tolerance to 00B.

Please add catalog ids for (a) Nepal IT-industry/independent export studies (e.g. IIDS) and (b) the Oxford Internet Institute Online Labour Index, rather than filing them under 'academic'. Allocate a network-enabled run to fetch leads 08A-L01..L03, L12, L14, L22.

Accepted: any services-export productivity assumption will state the ICT graduate flow it requires and be checked against your tertiary_profile; stock (employment) and flow (graduates) will not be added.

uncertainty: Very high. No values have been retrieved. Structural uncertainty: the size of unrecorded IT exports depends on channel and coverage definitions that are not yet documented; industry-estimated series are survey-based with undocumented sampling in the leads seen so far; AI effects by segment rest on non-Nepal evidence (24A). Occupational employment estimates at 4-digit ISCO may be statistically unreliable.

series.definition: NRB BPM6 services credits: telecommunications, computer and information services (EBOPS SI)
NRB monthly IT-service receipts memo series (definition to be confirmed and mapped to S1)
Survey-based IT export estimate (firms + freelancers), industry/independent study
series.note: Never merged with S1; S1 and S2 always reported side by side.

series.definition: UNCTADstat ICT services and digitally deliverable services exports
series.note: Derived from NRB BoP; not independent of S1.

series.definition: WTO modelled digitally delivered services exports

ict_export_series.method: Tabulate each series separately with vintage; convert NPR to USD only with a documented NRB average rate observation; convert FY to calendar year only via a documented method (e.g. monthly data) and never by averaging adjacent FYs silently.

components: Occupation x industry employment: NSO NLFS microdata (2017/18 completed; NLFS IV FY2024/25 onward when released) tabulated at ISCO-08 4-digit for 25xx, 35xx, 2166, 2513, 2643, 4131, 4132, 4222, 4229, 4311, crossed with ISIC Rev.4 61-63 and 82 and status in employment; report sample counts and standard errors (leads 08A-L14, L15).
Fallback: Census 2021 occupation-by-industry tables at the finest published level (08A-L16); NLSS IV 2022/23 as a cross-check with definitional caveats (08A-L17).
Freelancers: Online Labour Index supply-side counts and occupation mix for Nepal (08A-L22) and the industry study freelancer count (08A-L12), kept separate.

IT-export composition: segment and destination composition from the industry export study (08A-L12); if unavailable, a new structured survey of IT firms and freelancers would be required - design only, any fieldwork or contact needs recorded human approval.
Crosswalk: map industry-study segments to ISCO codes to allow ILO WP140 weighting; document the mapping as an assumption.

channels: Company exports received through banks and coded as computer services: captured in S1.
Freelancer receipts converted through banks/licensed FX dealers: may be coded as computer services, personal transfers or other; coding practice under NRB FX directives to be established (08A-L04).
Earnings kept abroad (platform balances, foreign bank/wallet accounts) or repatriated via informal channels: not captured in S1.
ITES/BPO, design and marketing: may be classed as other business services (SJ) or personal/cultural/recreational (SK) rather than SI; coverage alignment needed before any gap is computed.
Commercial presence (Mode 3) and Nepal-owned firms abroad: not exports under BPM6 residence rules; industry studies may include them.
recording_gap_notes.escalation: Gap beyond tolerance with unclear cause goes to 00B; no adjustment of NRB figures.

segment_outlook.method: Combine 24A causal/exposure evidence (automation vs augmentation) with 24C global demand by EBOPS segment; grade evidence per 24A hierarchy; no segment labelled growth or displacement in r1.
segment_outlook.competition_note: Comparator suppliers (India, Philippines, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan) to be benchmarked with UNCTADstat calendar-year series (08A-L05) - pending.
